clue.text: Blow up about a pound of aggregate

indicators.note: about means the explosion word is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: to blow up is to blast
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to blow something up over a pound's worth of gravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and L (pound) inside BLAST. 'aggregate' is the noun: crushed stone or gravel used as weight or bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy gravel or stone used as bulk material, which is what aggregate is.

clue.text: Miss Derek's fine biographer

parts.note: the actress Bo Derek; her possessive gives BO plus S
well means fine, in good health

explanation.surface: An actress's excellent life-writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo Derek is an American film actress; her possessive gives BOS. James Boswell wrote the celebrated life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson, the classic English literary life story.

clue.text: Sinister inclination

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, so a leaning to the left side rather than an evil tendency

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' suggests wickedness, but its Latin root means left; the inclination is a natural preference for one hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant on the left, so a tendency towards the left hand is a preference for it.

clue.text: Hurt by a cold man

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A chilly man is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt with a dull persistent pain.

clue.text: Agent is in trouble for causing harassment

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of agent is are disturbed and jumbled

explanation.surface: A spy gets into difficulty for pestering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' signals an anagram of AGENT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing is mocking or provoking someone playfully, a mild form of tormenting.

clue.text: Honour an Arabian state

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An Arabian country receives a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the south-east of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Letters for delivery from the station

definitions.meaning: a remote military or trading base

explanation.surface: Mail goes out from the depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as OUT POST, mail waiting to go out; 'from the' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote station or settlement, and post that is going out is mail awaiting delivery.

clue.text: Top-class US lawyer produced Verdi opera

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An excellent American attorney staged a Verdi work.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, with 1 as I; DA is a US District Attorney. 'produced' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's 1871 opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Duty to disclose regular practices

definitions.meaning: habits or traditions, things usually done

explanation.surface: It is one's duty to reveal habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disclose' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are both import duties levied at a border and traditional ways of behaving.

clue.text: Sail on and on to find Utopia

definitions.meaning: a voyage that never reaches the shore

explanation.surface: Keep voyaging to reach paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: a ship that never, never lands sails on and on. 'to find' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of Peter Pan is an idealised imaginary place, and a ship that never makes port sails on forever.

clue.text: Often sheds tears out of compassion

indicators.note: out of here signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who cries a lot does so from kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' signals the anagram. The surface reads 'out of compassion' as a reason for crying; it splits as indicator plus definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is kindly sympathy, the quality of having a tender, feeling nature.

clue.text: Resounding notes from the chorus

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken from within the words the chorus

explanation.surface: Ringing sounds come from a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters lying across 'the chorus'.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated back by reflection, a resounding of notes.

clue.text: Nothing about former US president

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Nothing is said about a past American leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States, resigning in 1974.

clue.text: Leading man wins the lady's love

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady
love is zero in tennis, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: The romantic lead wins over the woman's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like O; 'wins' just joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the principal male character in a film or play.

clue.text: My Italo-French friend in Florida

parts.note: mi is a Romance word for my
ami is French for friend, also the start of Italian amico

explanation.surface: My continental friend is in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: AMI is French for friend and begins the Italian amico, hence 'Italo-French'; MI is 'my' in Romance languages such as Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city located in Florida, so it is something found in that state.

clue.text: Make confused theologian get stuck into the drink

indicators.note: get stuck into means the theologian goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian gets into the beer and becomes muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get stuck into' is the container signal; 'theologian' gives the Doctor of Divinity degree, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or befuddle someone's mind.

clue.text: Coming down from the top of the stairs

definitions.meaning: the act of descending to the ground, as an aircraft does
the level floor area at the head of a staircase

explanation.surface: Someone descends from the head of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane's descent to earth and the flat space at the head of a flight of steps share one word.

clue.text: Information ebbs and flows!

definitions.meaning: jokingly read as tide-ings, things the tides do

explanation.surface: News comes and goes like the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the tide ebbs and flows, so the word is read as 'tide-ings'; the exclamation mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings are news, and the word puns on the rise and fall of the sea's tides.

clue.text: Say nothing to support a parent

definitions.meaning: read literally, to provide for one's mother

explanation.surface: Advice to stay quiet while providing for a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for keeping a secret also reads literally as maintaining one's mother financially.

clue.text: The type to be influenced and inspired

parts.note: kind means type or sort
led means guided or influenced

explanation.surface: The sort who is easily swayed and motivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' and 'and' only join the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindled means aroused or stirred up, as interest or enthusiasm is inspired.

clue.text: Keep tabs on an ass in upland area

indicators.note: in shows the ass word placed within the upland word

parts.note: a moor is high open land
a nit is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Watch a donkey on the high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' suggests a donkey but means a fool; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to watch or check on something regularly.

clue.text: Fuss made by father in front of the basin

indicators.note: in front of means the father word is placed before the basin word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a laver is a large washing basin, as in old churches or the Bible

explanation.surface: Dad makes a scene in front of the washbasin.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means tiresome fuss and bother over something trivial.

clue.text: Retire and move into the fast lane

definitions.meaning: withdraw, as troops or a competitor do
steer out from behind to overtake

explanation.surface: Stop working and drive faster.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out is to withdraw from something, and also to swing out into the outer lane of a road.

clue.text: Put in mechanical performance, for award

indicators.note: in places the put word within the performance word

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition without thought
set means put or placed

explanation.surface: Someone does a routine show to win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'for' only links to the definition, a prize ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize, at shows for instance.

clue.text: A number at home in the Durham area

indicators.note: in places the at-home word within the area's abbreviation

parts.note: County Durham is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone is counted at home in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: County Durham lies in the North East region of England; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a cardinal number, one more than eight.

clue.text: Fish fork

definitions.meaning: a verb, to fish with rod and line
a noun, a branching point or corner where two lines meet

explanation.surface: Two words: a fish and a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a hook, and an angle is the corner formed where two lines diverge, as at a fork.

clue.text: British sailors enter American vessels

indicators.note: enter means the sailors go inside the American abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: Royal Navy men board United States ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' looks like ships, matching the sailors, but here means containers such as vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, so they are vessels in the sense of pots.

clue.text: Syrian bishop unaffected by reversal

indicators.note: unaffected by reversal says the letters read the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern cleric does not change when turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: Abba, meaning father, is a title of bishops in the Syriac churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba, meaning father, is the title given to bishops and patriarchs in Syriac Christianity.

clue.text: Whence Napoleon saw fit to return

definitions.text: Whence Napoleon saw fit to return

indicators.note: to return means the fit word is read backwards

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: The island the French emperor chose to come back from.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon escaped from exile on Elba in 1815 to return to France, so the whole clue describes the island as well as giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island Napoleon left in 1815 to regain power in France.

clue.text: Of equal value at the end

definitions.text: Of equal value at the end

parts.words: Of equal value at the end
parts.note: a stock phrase said of the final person or item named, meaning it matters as much as those before

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: the phrase used when introducing the final item in a list, insisting it is no less important.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces the final item while insisting it matters as much as the rest.

clue.text: Lovely show by trade

definitions.meaning: an exhibition put on by an industry, a trade exhibition

explanation.surface: A beautiful exhibition put on by business.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means beautiful in old-fashioned usage, and a trade fair is an exhibition held by an industry.

clue.text: The leader with a duck-like gait? Rubbish!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of The

parts.note: a waddle is the rolling walk of a duck

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a chief who walks like a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The leader' is the first letter of 'The', T; 'with' joins it to WADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly nonsense, so the exclamation means much the same as calling something nonsense.
